purpose: Crosswalk the Cagayan B0380 basin candidate Stigmatogobius elegans to its original species description, type series, Smithsonian holotype record, later Philippine type checklist, and newly reviewed local Pared/Cagayan hydrology context without treating that context as an exact type-site coordinate.

candidate.globalDatasetRole: Basin-level discovery candidate; numeric bibliography referenceIds are not a verified citation-to-basin crosswalk.

originalDescription.citation: Larson, H. K. (2005). A revision of the gobiid genus Stigmatogobius (Teleostei: Gobiidae), with descriptions of two new species. Ichthyological Exploration of Freshwaters, 16(4), 347-370.

holotype.reportedLocality: Dry-season pool, 2 m deep, separated from the main channel of the Imurung River by 10 m, Barrio San Miguel, Cagayan Province, Luzon

paratypes.localityRelation: Same data as holotype; cleared and stained

paratypes.reportedLocality: Main channel of the Imurung River, Barrio San Miguel, Cagayan Province; original paper spells municipality as Bagao

originalDescription.historicalDistributionStatement: The 2005 description says known only from Luzon and freshwater in a single river system, in shallow flowing water over sand and pebble substrate.
originalDescription.interpretationLimit: This is a dated historical type-series record, not evidence of current presence or a current range assessment.

laterTypeChecklist.citation: Balisco, R. A. T., & Liao, T.-Y. (2025). An annotated checklist of fish species described from the Philippines. ZooKeys, 1246, 1-287, treatment 416, printed pp. 94-95.
laterTypeChecklist.license: CC BY 4.0, as recorded for the existing source-registry entry balisco-liao-2025-philippine-fish-described-checklist
laterTypeChecklist.crossCheck: The checklist repeats the USNM 314469 holotype locality/date and identifies USNM 376152, NTM 15807-001 and USNM 314213 as paratypes. It prints Bagao for the municipality of USNM 314213, while the Smithsonian indexed holotype record and other sources use Baggao. Preserve the spelling difference; it does not change the type locality crosswalk.

localityResolution.reportedLocality: Barrio San Miguel, Baggao Municipality, Cagayan Province, Luzon
localityResolution.basinCrosswalk: The primary description and Smithsonian record identify Imurung River, Barrio San Miguel, Cagayan Province, but supply no coordinate. The NCCA Duba Rivers and Caves entry says local waters flow to Pared River and support irrigation in San Miguel and Imurung; the Cagayan Riverine Zone Development Framework Plan identifies Pared River as a major Cagayan River tributary. This provides indirect local network context consistent with the Cagayan basin, but no reviewed source explicitly connects the Imurung type reach itself to Pared or locates that reach. Exact membership in global polygon B0380 remains unverified.
localityResolution.evidenceClass: Historical voucher/type-locality record, georeferenced only to named river and administrative locality in the reviewed sources.

localContext.source: National Commission for Culture and the Arts, Talapamana entry for Duba Rivers and Caves, Baggao
localContext.reportedConnection: The entry says running water from the Duba cave system goes to Pared River and describes Pared River as the irrigation source for rice lands in San Miguel, Imurung, San Francisco, and San Jose.

parentBasinContext.source: Cagayan Riverine Zone Development Framework Plan 2005-2030, NEDA Region II/DEPDev Region II
parentBasinContext.reportedConnection: The plan includes Pared River among the major tributaries in the Cagayan Riverine Zone and explicitly notes that some northeast/northwest Cagayan watersheds do not drain through the Cagayan River.

hydrologyCrosswalk.interpretation: The local and parent-basin sources support a plausible Pared-to-Cagayan hydrological context near the administrative locality, but they do not document the Imurung type reach's direct confluence path or exact position. Province, barangay, and nearby water-system references are not substitutes for a georeferenced fish voucher.
hydrologyCrosswalk.geometryAction: No coordinate or point-in-polygon result added; exact Imurung-to-Pared link and B0380 membership remain pending.

recentSurveyLead.reportStatement: The 2026 Nagao Foundation survey report says Stigmatogobius elegans was observed in Cagayan and that collected material would be examined for taxonomy, phylogeny, coloration and distribution.
recentSurveyLead.localityPrecision: Province-level Cagayan only; no taxon-specific field date, exact river/reach, coordinate, or specimen catalog accession is supplied in the report.
recentSurveyLead.crosswalkToImurungTypeSeries: No evidence connects the 2026 observation/material to the 1989 Imurung River type series.
recentSurveyLead.rightsStatus: No item-specific reuse license was identified in the earlier source review.
recentSurveyLead.evidenceClass: Recent source-reported observation lead, not a map-ready occurrence or independently voucher-verified record.

gbifCrossCheck.interpretation: The zero-coordinate result is a bounded GBIF indexing outcome. It does not negate the historical named-river voucher record or establish biological absence.

interpretation: The primary description and official Smithsonian catalog record independently anchor the species' historical type series to the Imurung River in Cagayan Province, with a collection date of 2 May 1989.

A separate 2026 Nagao Foundation report says the species was observed in Cagayan, but provides only province-level locality and no taxon-specific date, exact waterbody, coordinate, or specimen accession; it is not linked to the 1989 type series.

NCCA describes Duba waters going to Pared River and supporting irrigation for San Miguel/Imurung lands; the regional Cagayan Riverine Zone plan includes Pared among Cagayan River tributaries. This supports indirect local basin context but does not explicitly connect the Imurung type reach to Pared.

No reviewed source gives a type-site coordinate or exact Imurung-to-Pared connection, so point-in-polygon testing and exact B0380 membership remain unresolved. Cagayan Province alone is insufficient because the regional plan notes some Cagayan watersheds do not drain through the Cagayan River.
The global basin candidate remains a discovery lead; this review does not claim the Imurung type locality lies inside B0380 or that the taxon is currently present there.
No species, occurrence, geometry, diet, bait, catchability, legal, safety, or public-app row is created by this research crosswalk.

sourcePolicy.rightsReview: The original paper is copyrighted by the publisher and no item-specific reuse grant was verified. The 2025 checklist is CC BY 4.0. The 2026 report has no item-specific reuse terms in the reviewed source note. No derived public app row is approved.
sourcePolicy.qualityReview: The type series anchors a historical event and locality; the 2026 report adds only a province-level observation lead. Neither establishes exact coordinates, B0380 membership, abundance, catchability, legal status, or safety.
sourcePolicy.accessEvidence: The original publisher PDF and peer-reviewed checklist were directly read. Smithsonian item details came from its official indexed search record; a full museum record and coordinate were not retrieved. The 2026 project report was directly reviewed in an earlier source assessment. NCCA's local Duba-to-Pared description and the regional Cagayan Riverine Zone plan were directly reviewed for indirect hydrological context; neither supplies the type-site coordinate or explicit Imurung-to-Pared linkage.
